title: Zotero Web API Documentation
author: Zotero
snippet: Zotero desktop exposes a local API; the Web API supports library items, collections, tags, versioned incremental retrieval with since/Last-Modified-Version, and writable JSON through authenticated requests.
claims: Zotero can serve as a bibliographic source of truth and incremental sync endpoint.

title: How Obsidian stores data
author: Obsidian
snippet: Obsidian stores notes as Markdown plain-text files in a local vault and refreshes when external tools modify those files.
claims: Obsidian is suitable as a human-readable output and knowledge layer for external automation.

title: Properties
author: Obsidian
snippet: Obsidian properties store typed, machine-readable metadata in YAML frontmatter, while nested structures and bulk editing are better handled by scripts or other tools.
claims: Markdown notes can expose small structured fields while complex state remains better suited to a database.

title: Obsidian Zotero Integration
author: obsidian-community
snippet: The plugin imports citations, bibliographies, Zotero notes, and PDF annotations into Obsidian and integrates with citation-key tooling.
claims: Researchers have established a Zotero-to-Obsidian bridge for literature notes and citations.

title: ZotFlow — Keep Your Research in Flow
author: Xianpi Duan
snippet: ZotFlow implements bidirectional Zotero sync, one template-generated Markdown source note per item, offline caching, annotation handling, and conflict-aware synchronization inside Obsidian.
claims: A current implementation treats Zotero as the library and Obsidian as an active reading and note workspace.

title: read-summarize-papers
author: Angelamer
snippet: The project runs arXiv and Zotero ingestion into SQLite, applies two-tier relevance processing, deduplicates by DOI/arXiv/title/content hash, writes structured Obsidian notes, and stores processing state and run logs.
claims: A public personal project now implements almost the same pipeline as the current workspace.

title: ResearchPilot: A Local-First Multi-Agent System for Literature Synthesis and Related Work Drafting
author: Peng Zhang
snippet: ResearchPilot retrieves from Semantic Scholar and arXiv, extracts structured findings, synthesizes across papers, and persists history in a local-first stack using SQLite and Qdrant; it notes limits such as abstract-only extraction and missing citation verification.
claims: A second independent system uses staged extraction and local persistence rather than one-shot summarization.

title: PaperQA2
author: Future House
snippet: PaperQA2 indexes local scientific PDFs, fetches redundant metadata, chunks and ranks evidence, and produces citation-grounded answers; prior answers and indexes are persisted for later search.
claims: Full-text evidence indexing is a separate layer from bibliography and per-paper summaries.

title: Synthesizing scientific literature with retrieval-augmented language models
author: Asai et al.
snippet: OpenScholar combines a scientific data store, retriever, citation-backed synthesis, and a self-feedback inference loop, showing the importance of retrieval grounding and citation checking.
claims: Reliable multi-paper synthesis benefits from a persistent corpus, retrieval, and citation-aware feedback rather than free-form model memory.

title: ASReview LAB
author: ASReview
snippet: ASReview provides duplicate handling, saved screening decisions, active learning, and a workflow where the human remains the oracle for relevance judgments.
claims: Automated prioritization is commonly separated from final human inclusion decisions.

title: AI for Auto-Research: Roadmap & User Guide
author: Kong et al.
snippet: The review finds AI strongest on structured, retrieval-grounded, tool-mediated work and fragile on novelty and scientific judgment, recommending human-governed collaboration.
claims: Research automation should preserve human control over scientific judgment.
